language.howToChooseYourGradeIntro: Our curriculum Grades K to 6 corresponds with ages:
language.howToChooseYourGradeContent:
It’s very important children start at the right level, have fun in learning and work at their own pace. Please help the children selecting the level that is not too easy, but also not too difficult for them. There are two ways to do this.

  • You can either check the learning goals yourself to determine the correct level for your child(ren).
  • Or you can let the child take several lessons to determine his or her level. For example, if your child has the age of 6, please let him or her take one lesson in grade K, one lesson in grade 1, and one lesson in grade 2 to determine at which level he or she is.

dialog.text: Hello, I am Tim.
Hi, my name is Sarah. I love to dive, and I love history!

In school, we learned about the Lighthouse of Alexandria. It was one of the seven wonders of the ancient world and was destroyed by earthquakes hundreds of years ago. This fort is made from some of its remains.
Divers sometimes find relics of the lighthouse under the water near it! I think it would be exciting to find a relic, but I have never tried to find one before.
I know divers sometimes use magnets to search for relics, but I don't know much about magnets. Can you help me learn about magnets so I can start searching?
Let's help Sarah learn about magnets!

I did some experiments with magnets and discovered some really interesting things. I will show you the pictures I took of my experiments. Can you guess what happened and why?

helperSimple.text: Read the questions about Sarah's experiments and choose the answers that explain what happened and why.

activities.title: Click on the correct option.
activities.subtitle: I tried to pick up a paperclip with the middle of the magnet. Did it work?

answers.text: Yes, the middle of the magnet is the strongest part.
No, the middle of a magnet is the weakest part.

activities.title: Click on the correct option.
activities.subtitle:
I put a paperclip 25 centimeters away from a magnet.
Did the magnet attract the paperclip?

answers.text: No, magnets only work if they are very close to the item.

activities.title: Click on the correct option.
activities.subtitle:
Compasses are made of magnets. I heard compasses
always point north. Do you think that is true?

answers.text: Yes, compasses always point north because the Earth is magnetized, and magnets naturally point to the North Pole.
No, compasses do not always point north.

activities.title: Click on the correct option.
activities.subtitle:
I put a paperclip inside a glass jar and used a magnet to try
to pick up the paperclip from outside the glass jar.
Did it work?

answers.text: Yes, magnetism can pass through non-magnetic objects.
No, magnet don't work through glass.

outro.text: Thanks for helping me understand how my experiments worked! Magnets are so interesting!
